rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient covering nearly the full solvent-strength range at mid temperature to reveal the overall retention window, whether any compounds are unretained or still trapped at 42 min, and where the peak density sits. A 20 min gradient is a balanced first pass that should expose enough selectivity and slope behavior to guide narrowing the phi window and adjusting steepness in the next injections.

All 10 compounds are already fully resolved; the only loss is time, so trim the gradient to the actual elution window and steepen it to pull the last peak earlier while keeping enough margin around the estimated elution compositions. The first and last peaks correspond to roughly phi_e about 0.11 and 0.59, so a 0.10-0.55 window with a shorter 10 min gradient should test whether we can keep everything resolved and move t_last toward 10 min.

We still have full resolution margin, so the next move is to shorten retention further by raising temperature and making the gradient slightly steeper while keeping the last peak inside the gradient window. Using phi1 0.60 preserves coverage for the last compound, and this test will show whether we can push t_last to about 10 min without collapsing the close mid-run cluster.

Injection 3 showed the close pair is highly sensitive to the more aggressive conditions, so back off slightly on both temperature and gradient steepness while keeping the run under 10 min if possible. This should recover resolution for pair 6/7 with only a modest retention increase, probing the tradeoff near the optimum.

The key pair degrades sharply at higher temperature and steeper conditions, but injection 4 overcorrected on time; an intermediate setting should improve the 6/7 resolution relative to injection 3 while keeping t_last closer to 10 min. Holding the same phi window isolates the temperature/steepness tradeoff near the current optimum.

The troublesome 6/7 pair barely improved with longer tG at the same phi window, suggesting it is not very slope-responsive there and may benefit more from shifting the composition window. Lowering phi1 slightly should move the crowded mid-elution region to a gentler effective solvent range while keeping the run fast enough to preserve a strong time score.

The close pair is not improved by narrowing or flattening the window, so test the opposite composition shift at the best-temperature fast conditions: move the window slightly higher in phi while keeping the short gradient that gave the top CRF. This probes whether pair 6/7 responds to a different effective solvent-strength region rather than to slope alone, while preserving the favorable sub-10 min last peak.

Raising phi1 from 0.60 to 0.65 improved both time and the critical 6/7 pair, so continue that trend with a slightly stronger upper composition at the same fast, high-temperature conditions. This tests whether the pair keeps separating in this shifted phi region without sacrificing the excellent sub-10 min last peak.

The last two increases in phi1 both improved the critical 6/7 resolution while further shortening the run, so keep stepping upward to map that trend. At unchanged tG and T this cleanly tests whether the pair continues to benefit from a higher phi window and whether CRF can climb further toward the limit set by that one pair.

The monotonic improvement in the 6/7 pair and CRF as phi1 rises suggests the crowded region is moving into a more favorable selectivity window, with no time penalty because all peaks remain well before 10 min. Continue the one-variable sweep to see whether this trend persists toward higher phi1.

The CRF and the critical 6/7 resolution have improved steadily with each increase in phi1, while all peaks remain comfortably before 10 min. One more upward step should show whether that trend continues or starts to reverse as the window becomes very strong.

The upward phi1 sweep continues to improve the only subcritical pair with no time penalty, so the most informative next step is to keep following that monotonic trend. This checks whether selectivity for pair 6/7 keeps getting better closer to the high-organic limit.

The critical pair has improved monotonically across the phi1 sweep from 0.60 to 0.90, so the next logical move is to test the upper grid limit. This will show whether the selectivity gain continues at the strongest allowed window and may further raise the CRF.

Phi1 = 0.90 was the best composition window, and phi1 = 0.95 introduced a second weak pair, so keep phi1 at 0.90 and now test a slightly shallower gradient. Since all peaks already elute far before 10 min, lengthening tG from 8 to 10 min sacrifices no time score but may improve the remaining critical 6/7 pair toward full credit.

At phi1 = 0.90 the close pair worsened when tG was lengthened, so it is behaving more like a temperature/selectivity problem than a slope problem. Lowering T from 50 to 45 at the best composition window should test whether that pair gains enough selectivity to outweigh any modest increase in retention, which should still stay under 10 min.

Temperature and longer tG both hurt the key pair at the best high-phi window, so the remaining useful lever is the low-end composition. Raising phi0 should shift the crowded early-middle region to a different effective solvent-strength segment while keeping the run very short, testing whether pair 6/7 responds to the lower bound rather than phi1 alone.

Raising phi0 from 0.10 to 0.15 improved the critical 6/7 pair past 1.0, so continue that direction to see if the low-end window shift can push it closer to full credit. The first peak is still retained at 0.86 min, so there is room to raise phi0 one more step without obviously losing compounds.

Phi0 = 0.15 helped pair 6/7 but phi1 = 0.90 still left some crowding and phi0 = 0.20 created an overly early weak 4/5 pair, so combine the better lower bound with a slightly milder upper bound. This targets a compromise composition window that may improve both vulnerable pairs simultaneously while keeping all peaks well under 10 min.

The best result came from phi0 = 0.15, and reducing phi1 from 0.90 to 0.85 improved the balance between the two weak pairs, so step phi1 down once more at the same fast conditions. This tests whether the compromise window can further equalize 4/5 and 6/7 and raise the overall capped-resolution average.

The best composition window so far is 0.15 to 0.85, and moving phi1 lower did not improve the limiting 6/7 pair, so now revisit slope at this better window. Because t_last is still far below 10 min, a slightly longer gradient costs no time score and could raise the weakest pair enough to beat the current best.

At the best window, making the gradient longer worsened the limiting pair, so test the opposite direction: a slightly steeper gradient. Since all peaks are still well before 10 min, shortening tG can be explored without time risk and may sharpen the local selectivity pattern enough to improve 6/7.

The best region is clearly around phi0 0.15 and tG 8, and changes in slope or lower temperature have been unfavorable, so the one remaining strong lever is a higher temperature at that improved low-end window. A modest increase to 55 C may shift selectivity enough to help the persistent 6/7 pair while retention is already safely below the 10 min threshold.

Higher temperature at phi1 = 0.90 shifted the weak spot from 6/7 to a nearly coeluting 4/5 pair, suggesting 55 C changes selectivity strongly in this region. Testing 55 C at the current best window, phi0 0.15 to phi1 0.85, checks whether backing off phi1 restores 4/5 while preserving any gain for 6/7.

The only major lever not yet tested at the best composition window is the maximum temperature. Although 55 C hurt 4/5, a final boundary test at 60 C could reveal a non-monotonic selectivity shift and is the most informative distinct method left near the current optimum.

A higher temperature shifted the limiting selectivity from pair 6/7 to pair 4/5, and stronger high-organic windows tend to help that earlier region under the hottest conditions. For the final shot, combine the 60 C selectivity shift with a higher phi1 and shorter gradient to test whether pair 4/5 opens enough while all peaks remain comfortably before 10 min.
